title: Grilled polenta wedges
subtitle: Crisp-edged polenta cut into wedges and grilled
excerpt: Soft polenta poured into a tin, chilled until firm, cut into wedges, and grilled until golden and slightly charred. Serve with roasted vegetables, braises, or a sauce. A versatile side that repurposes leftover polenta brilliantly.
sourceNotes: Firm polenta cut and grilled (or pan-fried) is a standard preparation across northern Italy, used wherever soft polenta would be served. Cross-referenced with Giorgio Locatelli, Made in Italy (2006).

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the wedges on a tray before the grilling stage, then bag and freeze for up to 3 months. Grill directly from frozen.
recipe.batchNotes: Make a large batch, chill, and portion. Grill wedges as needed.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Polenta must be made and set a minimum of 1 hour ahead (or overnight).

content.text: Grilled polenta wedges start with the same soft polenta as the soft version but are poured out thinner and left to set solid. Grilling gives the exterior a golden crust while the inside stays creamy. They are a versatile side dish that can be prepared entirely ahead and grilled to order.

Bring the water to the boil with the salt. Pour in the polenta in a thin stream, whisking constantly. Reduce heat and cook, stirring often, for 30 to 35 minutes until very thick and pulling away from the sides of the pan.

Remove from heat. Beat in the butter and Parmesan. Pour immediately into a lightly oiled baking tray (about 30 x 20 cm) to a depth of about 1.5 cm. Smooth the top with a wet spatula. Leave to cool, then refrigerate for at least 1 hour until completely firm.
Turn the set polenta out onto a board. Cut into triangles or rectangles. Brush with olive oil on both sides.

Heat a griddle pan or heavy frying pan to high heat. Grill the polenta pieces for 3 to 4 minutes per side without moving them, until they have charred grill marks and a golden crust. They should release cleanly when ready.

items.symptom: The polenta sticks to the griddle
items.cause: Pan not hot enough or polenta moved too soon
items.fix: Heat the griddle until very hot before adding polenta. Do not move it; it will release when a crust forms.

items.symptom: The polenta didn't set firm enough to cut
items.cause: Not chilled long enough or too much liquid in the polenta
items.fix: Chill overnight. The polenta should be as firm as cold butter.
Season the cooking water generously. Add more Parmesan. A drizzle of good olive oil and flaked salt after grilling helps.

items.symptom: The surface is burnt but the inside is still cold
items.cause: Polenta straight from fridge on a very high heat
items.fix: Let the wedges come to room temperature for 15 minutes before grilling, or use medium-high heat and cook slightly longer.

content.text: Firm grilled polenta is the other form of polenta in northern Italian cooking, the contrast to the soft, creamy version. Where soft polenta is a comfort food and the base for ragù and stews, grilled polenta is a side dish, an antipasto, or a platform: it can be topped with mushrooms, gorgonzola, caramelised onion, or roasted peppers. It is also the thing to do with leftover soft polenta, which sets in the pot and can be cut the next day and grilled or pan-fried.
